Pull a single column from a GPU table

Source: R/pull.R
pull.tbl_gpu.Rd

Extracts one column as a plain R vector, similar to dplyr::pull(). Materializes any pending lazy operations first via compute(), then collect()s the table and picks out the requested column.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
pull(.data, var = -1, name = NULL, ...)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

var

A variable, as a name, position (positive or negative, counting from the end), or expression evaluated against column positions (see dplyr::pull()'s own contract). Defaults to the last column.

name

An optional column (by the same rules as var) whose values become the names of the returned vector.

...

Not used; for extensibility, must be empty.

Value

A plain R vector (not a tbl_gpu), named if name was supplied. Grouping (if any) is ignored, matching dplyr::pull().

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)
  gpu_mtcars |> pull(mpg)
}
#>  [1] 21.0 21.0 22.8 21.4 18.7 18.1 14.3 24.4 22.8 19.2 17.8 16.4 17.3 15.2 10.4
#> [16] 10.4 14.7 32.4 30.4 33.9 21.5 15.5 15.2 13.3 19.2 27.3 26.0 30.4 15.8 19.7
#> [31] 15.0 21.4
